lines.text: Feeling behind is two thousand years old.
Nearly two thousand years ago, the Roman philosopher Seneca wrote about it.
Most people, he wrote, complain that life is too short, that it ends just as they're getting ready to live.
Sound familiar? Nineteen, scrolling at two in the morning, sure everyone else started without you.
Seneca's answer wasn't what they wanted to hear.
"It is not that we have a short space of time, but that we waste much of it."
It sounds harsh. Read it again.
He isn't saying you failed. He's saying the time is still there.
Most of it doesn't disappear in big mistakes. It slips away in small hours nobody chose.
The scroll you didn't even enjoy. The plan you keep moving to Monday.
His advice was to guard your hours the way you'd guard anything else that's yours.
One hour tonight that you choose on purpose: a page, a walk, a call, a first try.
You're not behind. You're taking your time back.

post.caption: Seneca wrote this almost 2,000 years ago, and it still lands. What would you do with one hour that's fully yours? 🌅
post.pinned_comment: Be honest: where does your 2 a.m. hour usually go? 👇
